newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.

text.p: Indian sub-continent gold prices are expected to be under pressure in the next few days on improved supplies and poor demand, dealers said on Monday.
They said last week's sharp fall in world gold prices could increase the flow of metal into both India, the world's largest consumer of gold, and its neighbour, Pakistan, in the coming few days.
In the week to Monday, gold fell 25 rupees to 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes on the Bombay bullion market after losing 95 rupees in the previous week.
Bombay dealers said gold's fall to around $340 per ounce in international markets, its lowest since April 1993, had affected market sentiment in the sub-continent.
"Buyers are keeping to the sidelines, hoping for a further fall in prices because sizeable imports of gold are expected to arrive in the market soon," said Bombay dealer Mahavir Shah.
"I would expect demand to pick up at lower price levels," Shah said. " Gold can bounce back in the next few days with the help of some fresh buying."

India, which consumes nearly 500 tonnes of gold every year, including 300 tonnes of imported metal and 200 tonnes of recycled gold, is in the middle of a six-month-long wedding season, lasting up to May.

In Pakistan's commercial city of Karachi, dealers said they would expect gold prices to ease on higher supplies and lower demand for jewellery when trading resumes on Wednesday after the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holidays.
In the week to Sunday, gold fell 69 rupees per 10 grammes to 4,718 rupees on the Karachi bullion market.
